blocks.text: For its fourth edition, the Digital sector opens a new chapter under the curatorship of Marco De Mutiis, digital curator at the Fotomuseum Winterthur (Switzerland).
It brings together 13 contemporary art galleries, curatorial platforms and special projects around the transformations of the photographic image linked to digital technologies.

“If it is true that photography has shaped how we look at, interpret and construct the world for two hundred years, it is equally true that this photographic vision has never stopped transforming with technological change.

“After more than three decades of digital imagery intruding on the photographic medium, we no longer ‘see’ solely through the prism of optics. Our gaze is steeped in the layers of Photoshop as well as in the aesthetics specific to social media, facial recognition algorithms and internet memes. We interpret reality through selfie and mobile-phone culture, digital graphics and photorealistic artificial intelligence, screenshots and the ‘like’ economy. Our vision is augmented, extended and challenged by machines; photographic images have become spaces of collaboration and conflict between humans and non-humans.

“Many photographers and contemporary artists are exploring the photographic image and its transformations under digital and networked conditions, revealing in turn how these conditions shape our perception and the notions of authorship and mediation. Their practices question and extend the field of photography, highlighting the medium’s experimental potential by reinventing the formats, materials and techniques that push the image into unexplored territories.

“Continuing the essential work of Nina Roehrs, whose curatorial vision has established the Digital sector over the past three years as a space for artistic exploration and experimentation, the sector is opening a new chapter. My approach aims to deepen the dialogue between digital specificity and the long history of photography—highlighting continuities as much as ruptures, and paving the way for practices that challenge established aesthetic notions while honoring the effervescent, transformative spirit of the medium.

“In short, experimental and yet rooted in the photographic: works that push the limits of the medium while remaining open to exchange with its history, its materiality and its unshakable capacity to renew our way of seeing.

“As part of the Bicentennial of Photography, “The digital sector simultaneously reveals both its heritage and its future: from the medium’s origins—with a technology that revolutionized the way we see—to the emerging forms that will shape the way we see over the next two hundred years.”

Marco De Mutiis is a curator and digital curator at the Fotomuseum Winterthur (Switzerland), where he leads research on new forms of image production and circulation linked to algorithmic technologies and networked environments.

He recently co-curated the exhibitions The Lure of the Image and How to Win at Photography – Image-making as Play . He is also co-author of The Photographer’s Guide to Los Santos and co-editor of Screen Images – In-Game Photography, Screenshot, Screencast .
